verses.text: Then the people of the land took Josiah's son Jehoahaz and made him king in Jerusalem in place of his father.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he ruled for three months in Jerusalem.
The king of Egypt removed him from being king in Jerusalem. He made the land pay about three and a half tonnes of silver and thirty-four kilograms of gold.
The king of Egypt made Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz, Eliakim's brother, to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for eleven years in Jerusalem. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked him and bound him with bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the things from the LORD's temple to Babylon and put them in his temple there.
Everything else Jehoiakim did, the disgusting things he did, and all the evil found in him, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin became king after him.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled for three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did evil in the LORD's eyes.
In the spring, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon, along with valuable things from the LORD's temple. He made Jehoiachin's relative Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for eleven years in Jerusalem.
He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke the LORD's words.
He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him promise in God's name to be loyal. He was stubborn and refused to turn back to the LORD, the God of Israel.

All the leaders of the priests and the people also became more and more unfaithful. They followed all the disgusting practices of the nations, and they made the LORD's temple unclean, the temple he had made holy in Jerusalem.
The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent messages to them through his messengers again and again, because he had pity on his people and on the place where he lived.
But they made fun of God's messengers, hated his words, and laughed at his prophets. At last the LORD's anger rose against his people, and nothing could stop it.

So he brought the king of the Babylonians against them. He killed their young men with the sword in their holy temple. He had no pity on young men or young women, old people or the weak. God handed them all over to him.
He took to Babylon all the things from God's temple, large and small, the treasures of the LORD's temple, and the treasures of the king and his officials.
They burned God's temple and broke down the wall of Jerusalem. They burned all the palaces and destroyed everything of value.
He took the people who survived the sword away to Babylon. They became servants to him and his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to power.
This made the LORD's word through Jeremiah come true. The land finally enjoyed its Sabbath rests. All the time it lay empty, it rested, until seventy years were complete.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD made the message he spoke through Jeremiah come true. The LORD moved the heart of Cyrus king of Persia to send out an announcement all through his kingdom, and to write it down. It said:

"Cyrus king of Persia says: 'The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. He has chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem in Judah. Any of his people among you may go up there, and may the LORD their God be with them.'"
